value_memo:
RUBRIC WEIGHTING. Four pillars of roughly 25 points each, applied only to names that clear the forensic gate: (1) margin of safety, anchored on the chief risk officer's reconciled sum-of-the-parts discount (valuing each business line separately) and cross-checked against how many of the five valuation models agree, with any model reading on a peak or stale name discounted; (2) cyclical-peak versus durable-growth normalization applied before crediting any cheapness; (3) solvency judged on funded, interest-bearing debt against earnings plus interest coverage — the classic Altman score is ignored because it over-penalizes float and reserve businesses like insurers; (4) price against true, current peer multiples plus growth durability and returns on capital, so an optically cheap but structurally shrinking business is treated as a trap, not value. The catalyst overlay is fully removed: a live catalyst is neither a plus nor a requirement.

EXCLUSIONS AND CAPS. Excluded outright by the forensic gate (a management-credibility red flag the factor screen misses): BellRing Brands (BRBR), Dream Finders Homes (DFH), Peabody Energy (BTU), Corcept (CORT), Inspire Medical (INSP), Signify (LIGHT.AS), Molina Healthcare (MOH), Teleperformance (TEP.PA) and Hub Group (HUBG). Score-capped for credible-but-worsening trajectories: Porsche Holding (PAH3.DE), Pilgrim's Pride (PPC), TF1 (TFI.PA), FDJ United (FDJU.PA), Jungheinrich (JUN3.DE), Greenbrier (GBX), Photronics (PLAB), M6 Metropole (MMT.PA) and Carl Zeiss Meditec (AFX.DE). Called out explicitly as required: BellRing shows a +139% raw screen margin of safety with all five models positive, yet the deep dive on management scored at the exclusion line, the reconciliation produced no usable fair value at all, and the business carries funded debt at 4.2 times earnings with only 3.5 times interest coverage while the latest quarter fell 36% — the raw cheapness is not trustworthy, so it is out. Cal-Maine shows a +363% raw screen margin of safety, but the reconciled fair value is about $78 against an $81 price — roughly 3% of downside, not upside — because trailing earnings sit about nine times above the multi-year base on the avian-flu egg-price windfall and the latest quarter is down 90%; a low multiple on peak egg prices is not value. Also down-rated as peak or stale artifacts: Comcast (the spin-off re-rate already fired on a stale anchor — exited 2026-06-30), SM Energy (a 49% reconciled discount but interest coverage of only 0.5 times on stale peak energy earnings), Nvidia (reconciled discount of about 7% versus a +141% raw print), Abercrombie (earnings roughly seventeen times the multi-year base) and Chewy (stale numerator with only two models agreeing). Prosus and Progress Software were screened out on the franchise gate: both are flagged as earning below the cost of capital with eroding economics, which makes them ineligible regardless of headline cheapness, and Progress additionally carries funded debt at 4.3 times earnings with only 2.5 times coverage.

RISE AND FALL VERSUS THE PRIOR APEX (prior slate read from this file before overwriting: EEFT 84, WKL.AS 80, HRB 74, UHS 80, THC 73, NTES 79, SCR.PA 73, HRMY 72). EEFT 84 to 84, held at 1.1 units — still the best combination of discount (about 44%), five-of-five model agreement and clean funded leverage. WKL.AS 80 to 80, held at 0.8 units. HRB 74 to 74, held at 0.7 units. UHS 80 to 79, a hair lower on a slightly smaller reconciled discount (63% to 61%). THC 73 to 70 — the reconciled cushion is now only about 12% and the franchise screen half-caps it; the half unit stands. NTES 79 to 76 and resized from 1.1 to 0.5 units: only two of five models are positive and the raw screen reads negative, which makes the reconciled sum-of-the-parts the sole evidence of cheapness, and the sizing rule for such legs is a hard half unit — the parts method beats the five dissenting models here because it values the roughly 29%-of-market-value net cash and the games annuity separately, and the live peer tape (Tencent at fifteen to eighteen times free cash flow versus NetEase near twelve) corroborates the discount the ex-growth models miss. SCR.PA 73 to 73, held at 0.7 units. HRMY 72 to 70 on a stale, down-29% latest quarter and an eroding franchise trend; half unit stands. New seats: Lincoln National (72) enters at 0.7 units — never previously held, four of five models positive on a repairing life insurer at a 25% reconciled discount with a strengthening forensic read; Cognizant (76) enters at 0.6 units — it was held out of the prior slate for clustering with deflation-exposed services, and that hold-out is overridden this week in writing: a 42% reconciled discount on a net-cash business with four of five models agreeing is too much value to leave unseated, so it comes in at reduced size under an explicit combined cap that controls the cluster with numbers rather than avoidance. Prior runners-up Comcast and Deckers stay out (see runner-up notes).

CORRELATION STRESS (run over the final ten and argued against the measured two-year weekly numbers: average pairwise correlation 0.13, with UHS-THC at 0.68 the only pair above 0.6). (1) Hospital reimbursement — UHS and THC both ride the 2028 United States Medicaid directed-payment outcome and are the one measured pair above 0.6; both are kept because Universal Health is majority behavioral health while Tenet is increasingly ambulatory surgery, but a single ruling hits both, so they carry a numeric combined cap of 1.1 units. Ardent would re-cluster with this pair and was not used. (2) Advertising cycle — the Comcast plus Stroeer pair the rubric names is vacated: neither is seated this run. (3) AI-displacement theme — Wolters Kluwer and H&R Block, two names, sit exactly at the theme budget and carry a combined cap of 1.5 units; the Adobe, Gartner and Globant cluster is not seated (Adobe is first alternate only), and neither seated name here is a wide, non-eroding anchor that would count at half. (4) Broad AI narrative — Cognizant's billable-hour deflation is a different mechanism from seat-license displacement, but all three names de-rate on the same narrative tape, so a third, wider cap of 2.1 units spans WKL.AS, HRB and CTSH; this is the written justification for keeping the cluster rather than diversifying, with the alternative orthogonal name (Lincoln) seated separately anyway. (5) Payments disintermediation — Euronet is the sole leg; Pluxee is not seated because its discount to Edenred is shared Brazil and Italy regulatory beta (both peers de-rated on the same voucher reforms), which is sector beta rather than name-specific edge, so the gap was discounted rather than credited. (6) Rate and credit sensitivity — SCOR and Lincoln are both financials that would suffer together in a credit shock even though the drivers differ (catastrophe pricing versus rates and long-term-care reserves); combined cap 1.4 units; Swiss Re was avoided because it would re-cluster with SCOR in reinsurance. (7) Euro currency — Wolters Kluwer and SCOR share euro reporting; combined cap 1.5 units. Against the measured tape: the trailing numbers say these legs barely co-move today (average 0.13), so rather than merely asserting that, the caps are set as forward-looking factor controls sized off today's units — they bind the growth of each cluster, not just describe it.

BEAR REBUTTAL (one sentence per seat, written before final sizing). EEFT: if travelers abandon cash faster than the money-transfer and digital top-up legs grow, the ATM cash engine melts before the parts value is ever paid. WKL.AS: if generative AI answers legal, tax and clinical questions directly, subscription seats shrink and the EUR 82 fair value never re-rates. UHS: the $240 parts value rests on today's reimbursement peak, and one 2028 Medicaid ruling can reprice both hospital books at once. CTSH: AI-written code deflates billable hours across the whole offshore services model, so the 42% discount may simply be the market correctly pricing a shrinking revenue pool. NTES: if the three dissenting models are right that games cash flows are ex-growth, the net-cash pile is value trapped inside management's control, not shareholders'. HRB: free AI-assisted filing could do to paid tax preparation what free e-file did to storefront rivals, eroding the franchise faster than the 4.6% dividend compensates. SCR.PA: reinsurance pricing is at a hard-market peak, and one bad catastrophe year plus softening renewals sends earnings back to the normalized base while the discount closes downward. LNC: the long-term-care reserve hole has swallowed repaired-balance-sheet narratives before, and another assumption review breaks the $44 case. THC: earnings sit about three times above the multi-year base, so the thin 12% reconciled cushion can vanish in a single reimbursement print. HRMY: a one-drug company with generics circling — if the lifecycle-extension work fails, fair value decays toward net cash.

ROTATION (reconciled to the prior-decision ledger). KEEP EEFT — held since 2026-06-08, thesis intact, highest-conviction seat. KEEP WKL.AS — held since 2026-06-17, durable compounder, thesis intact. KEEP HRB — held since 2026-06-21, thesis intact. KEEP UHS — held since 2026-06-17, deepest hospital discount, thesis intact. KEEP THC — held since 2026-06-08, thesis intact though the cushion is thinner; half-capped by the franchise screen. KEEP NTES — held since 2026-06-17, thesis intact; resized to the half unit the sole-source-cheapness rule requires. KEEP SCR.PA — held since 2026-06-21, a clean financial anchor kept on pure-value grounds despite the debate grading it pass-for-now, a letter set partly under the now-removed catalyst overlay; the reconciled fair value of EUR 40 against roughly EUR 32, clean forensics and a 6% dividend stand on their own, and the peak-earnings question is already handled inside the reconciled number. KEEP HRMY — held since 2026-06-21, thesis intact but adds only into weakness. ADD LNC — never previously held; an orthogonal life-insurance leg. ADD CTSH — a prior runner-up promoted with the written override described above. No held name is dropped and no previously dropped name is re-added, so no thesis-change documentation is triggered this run; Booking and Abercrombie (dropped 2026-06-14), Adobe (dropped 2026-06-21) and Comcast (dropped 2026-06-30) all remain out precisely because no documented thesis change has arrived since their drop dates, and Deckers remains out because last run's adversarial review refuted its core reading and nothing new has surfaced.

SECULAR LOAD. book_secular_load_pct = 70 (seven of ten seats carry a material secular threat or an eroding franchise trend: EEFT, WKL.AS, HRB, UHS, THC, CTSH, HRMY); clean_anchor_count = 3 (NetEase, SCOR, Lincoln — 1.9 of 6.7 total units, about 28% of the book as ballast). Defense of the above-60% load: this is a deep-value book, so it structurally skews toward challenged names, but the load is spread across five distinct decline axes (AI displacement, labor deflation, payments disintermediation, hospital reimbursement, single-drug lifecycle), each held to a numeric combined cap; the measured average pairwise correlation of 0.13 — with only the hospital pair above 0.6, and that pair capped at 1.1 units — indicates the shared flight-to-quality factor is being controlled by sizing rather than assumed away, and the three clean anchors plus two dividend-paying financials provide ballast if the whole junk cohort de-rates together.
